description: Direct endpoint attack: attempt to inject authorization parameters via an unsigned (alg=none) OIDC request object; verify Dex rejects or does not accept the unsigned request object.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not consume authorization parameters from an unsigned request object (alg=none); the semantic proof (request object) must be authenticated under the intended policy before being applied.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object, indicating it may consume unauthenticated authorization parameters (proof integrity failure).
Dex returned a success status for an unsigned request object submission; it should reject or error on unauthenticated request objects.

description: Brokered-flow attack: attempt token exchange with missing/incorrect connector binding to see if Dex verifies the upstream proof under the wrong policy (connector). Includes a control exchange attempt and an attack exchange attempt.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify the submitted subject_token against the exact upstream connector policy selected by connector_id; it must not accept a token without correct connector binding or under an unintended verification context.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted token exchange without a valid connector_id, suggesting it may verify/consume the subject_token under an unintended or default policy (proof integrity failure).
Dex accepted token exchange using a non-OIDC connector_id, indicating it may not be applying the intended verification policy to the submitted proof.
Control token exchange failed with 401 (likely client auth/setup), making attack results inconclusive for proof-integrity testing.

description: Direct endpoint attack: attempt to substitute proof material in password grant by mixing identities and then verifying the granted identity; checks that Dex does not accept malformed/unauthenticated proof (e.g., empty password) and does not collapse into a valid session.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must only mint tokens when the exact credential proof (username/password) is authenticated; it must not accept empty/invalid proof or treat partial proof as valid.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an empty-password proof for password grant, indicating it may not be authenticating the exact semantic credential proof.
Dex accepted an incorrect password proof for password grant, indicating proof integrity failure.
Control password login did not yield a valid identity lookup, making proof-integrity attack results inconclusive.

description: Direct endpoint: attempt to smuggle/override authorization parameters via an unsigned (alg=none) request object and see if Dex accepts it (proof integrity of request object). Includes a baseline /auth request for comparison.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not consume authorization parameters from an unsigned request object (alg=none); if it does, it is verifying a different semantic proof than it consumes.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object or did not hard-fail it, indicating request object proof may be consumed without integrity verification.
Unsigned request object attempt resulted in a usable session identity, suggesting Dex consumed attacker-controlled authorization parameters without verifying the proof.

description: Brokered-flow: token exchange with a subject_token that uses attacker-controlled kid/untrusted signing key. Includes a control password login to prove the environment is functional and to compare identity behavior.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must reject upstream JWTs whose signature cannot be validated under the configured OIDC connector trust anchors (kid injection/untrusted key must not be accepted).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a token-exchange subject_token with attacker-controlled kid/untrusted signature, indicating proof verification did not match consumed semantics.
Dex produced a downstream identity/session from an untrusted-kid subject_token, suggesting signature verification bypass.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_control_pwd_login_status < 400 AND user_control_pwd_entity_id is not None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Control password login failed; token-exchange rejection/acceptance cannot be attributed to proof-integrity enforcement.

description: Brokered-flow: attempt trust-anchor substitution by presenting a JWT with a forged issuer and attacker-controlled JWKS semantics (simulated via mismatched iss) to the OIDC connector token exchange. Includes a control exchange attempt using a Dex-issued id_token as subject_token to ensure /token is reachable and client auth works.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must bind verification to the configured upstream issuer/trust anchors; a subject_token with a different issuer (even if well-formed) must be rejected and must not be consumed as a valid proof.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute attack outcome to proof-integrity enforcement versus setup/client-auth issues.
Dex accepted a subject_token with a forged issuer (trust-anchor substitution), indicating it may be consuming a proof not verified under the intended issuer/JWKS policy.
Dex produced a downstream identity from a forged-issuer subject_token, suggesting issuer/JWKS binding failure.

description: Authorization-code replay: exchange the same auth code twice (should be one-time use). Uses two identities to ensure the second exchange is not just a cached session.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: An OAuth2 authorization code is a one-time artifact and must not be accepted more than once, even if replayed immediately or by a different principal context.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was accepted more than once (replay succeeded); code should be one-time use.
Control exchange failed; cannot attribute replay outcome to anti-replay enforcement.

description: Refresh-token replay under rotation: obtain refresh_token, refresh once to rotate, then attempt to reuse the old refresh_token (should be rejected outside any reuseInterval). Uses two identities to ensure behavior is not user-specific.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Refresh tokens must not be reusable after rotation; reusing an older refresh token should be rejected (anti-replay) under default Dex rotation semantics.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control logins failed; refresh-token replay result may be due to setup rather than anti-replay.
Old refresh token was accepted after rotation (refresh-token replay succeeded); violates freshness/anti-replay.

description: Token-exchange replay: exchange the same upstream subject_token twice via the OIDC connector. If Dex treats the subject_token as a one-time artifact (or binds it to a single exchange), the second should be rejected; otherwise it indicates replay acceptance in the exchange path.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Token exchange should not allow replay of a one-time upstream proof artifact; if the upstream token is intended single-use (or Dex enforces one-time exchange), a second exchange should be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control subject_token acquisition failed; token-exchange replay result may be due to setup.
Same subject_token was accepted for token exchange more than once (replay succeeded); violates freshness/anti-replay expectations for one-time proof artifacts.

description: Authorization-code expiry enforcement: obtain an auth code, exchange it successfully (control), then attempt to exchange the same code again after the authRequests TTL window (simulated delay) to ensure it is rejected as expired/replayed.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes must not be reusable beyond their lifetime; a code accepted once must not be accepted again after TTL.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an authorization code replay after its intended lifetime (authRequests TTL) — code should be expired/one-time.

description: Refresh-token freshness after revocation: obtain refresh_token (control), revoke the session, then attempt to use the revoked refresh_token to mint new tokens; should be rejected.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Revoked credential artifacts (refresh tokens) must not be usable after revocation; replay after revocation should fail.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_alice_pwd_login_status == 200 AND user_bob_pwd_control_login_status == 200 AND alice_revoke_http_status == 200 AND user_alice_pwd_refresh_after_revoke_login_status >= 400
oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a refresh token after it was revoked — revoked artifacts must not be reusable.

description: Token-exchange replay after revocation: exchange a subject_token via OIDC connector (control), revoke the resulting Dex token, then attempt to exchange the same subject_token again; should be rejected if exchange artifacts are treated as one-time or bound to a live session.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Token-exchange should not allow replay of the same upstream subject_token after the derived session is revoked (anti-replay / freshness binding).

oracle_checks.assertion: user_control_pwd_login_status == 200 AND user_exchange_victim_login_status == 200 AND exchange_revoke_http_status == 200 AND user_exchange_replay_after_revoke_login_status >= 400
oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex allowed replay of the same upstream subject_token in token exchange even after the derived session was revoked — indicates missing freshness/anti-replay binding in exchange path.

description: Attempt to reuse the same refresh_token twice (back-to-back) to detect missing one-time semantics under refresh token rotation.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A refresh_token should not be reusable after it has been consumed to mint a new token (rotation). Reusing the same refresh_token twice should be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Old refresh_token was accepted a second time after being used once (rotation bypass / replay acceptance).
Control logins failed; refresh-token replay result is inconclusive due to environment/setup failure.

description: Token exchange: control exchange with a valid upstream subject_token, then attempt exchange with a subject_token that should be not-yet-valid (nbf far in the future).
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Dex must reject upstream JWTs that are not yet valid (nbf in the future) during token exchange; otherwise future-dated tokens can be replayed early.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; future-nbf rejection/acceptance is inconclusive due to connector/client auth/setup.
Dex accepted a not-yet-valid (future nbf) upstream JWT in token exchange, enabling early replay.

description: Obtain an authorization code, revoke the session before exchanging the code, then attempt to exchange the code. Code should not remain usable after revocation of the initiating session.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes are short-lived and should be invalidated when the initiating session is revoked; exchanging a code after revocation should be rejected (prevents replay of captured codes).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control authorization-code exchange failed; revoked-code exchange result is inconclusive.
Authorization code remained usable after revocation of the initiating session, enabling replay of captured codes.

description: Attack: reuse a Dex-issued access token (from password grant) after explicit revocation; token should no longer be accepted at /userinfo (anti-replay/freshness after revocation). Includes a control login to ensure the environment is functional.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: After a session/token is revoked, the revoked bearer token must not remain usable (no post-revocation replay).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control password-grant token was not accepted at /userinfo; test environment may be misconfigured (cannot interpret revocation replay result).
Revocation endpoint did not acknowledge revocation; cannot reliably test post-revocation replay.
Revoked access token remained usable at /userinfo (post-revocation replay accepted) — freshness/anti-replay violation.

description: OIDC code flow: start two auth requests (victim/attacker) with distinct state values, then attempt to exchange a code obtained under one state while presenting the other state's redirect_uri context (simulated by mismatched redirect_uri at /token). Tests cross-session splicing resistance.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the initiating auth request context (state/redirect_uri/session) and must not allow cross-session splicing or context swapping.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code redemption succeeded despite mismatched redirect_uri/context, indicating possible cross-session splicing or step-mixup in the code flow.

description: OIDC code flow: obtain an auth code (control), then attempt to redeem it without client authentication and without PKCE verifier (simulated by omitting code_verifier). Tests that the /token step cannot be completed out-of-protocol (step skipping / missing client binding).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The token endpoint must enforce the required bindings for code redemption (client authentication and/or PKCE when applicable) so the flow cannot be completed by skipping required steps.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token endpoint accepted an authorization code exchange without required client binding (e.g., missing client auth and/or PKCE), indicating step-skipping in the flow.

description: Token exchange: perform a control exchange with correct connector_id, then attempt an exchange using the same subject_token but with a different/incorrect connector_id to test whether the exchange is coherently bound to the selected upstream connector/session context.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Token exchange must be order-preserving and connector/session-bound; a subject_token minted/validated under one connector context must not be accepted under a different connector_id (no cross-connector splicing).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange accepted a subject_token under an incorrect connector_id, indicating cross-connector/session splicing and broken flow coherence.
Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute splice rejection/acceptance to flow-coherence enforcement.

description: Token exchange: perform a control exchange with correct connector_id, then attempt token exchange omitting connector_id to test that the multi-step exchange is bound to the selected upstream connector (no step skipping).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Token exchange must be order-preserving and bound to the correct upstream connector/session context. Omitting connector_id must not succeed, otherwise the flow can be completed out-of-protocol.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute subsequent failures/successes to flow-coherence enforcement.
Token exchange succeeded without connector_id, indicating the exchange flow is not coherently bound to an upstream connector/session context (step skipping).
A valid identity/session exists after token exchange without connector_id, suggesting connector-binding bypass.

description: OIDC auth-code flow: redeem the same authorization code twice to test one-time/atomic consumption and prevent step reordering/replay within the same client context.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be atomic and order-preserving; a code must not be redeemable more than once (no replay / step re-execution).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was redeemable more than once (second redemption succeeded), indicating non-atomic flow / replayable step.

description: RFC8693 token exchange: obtain a narrow-scope subject token, then attempt to exchange it for a broader scope without a fresh upstream authorization step (step skipping / non-atomic flow).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Multi-step exchange must be coherent and not allow skipping required upstream authorization steps to broaden scope within the same session/token context.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange allowed broadening scopes/claims without a fresh upstream authorization step, indicating non-atomic multi-step flow coherence failure.

description: OIDC authorization-code flow: attempt cross-session splicing by redeeming a code from session A while using session B's state (state swap / code injection).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be coherently bound to the initiating session via state; a code issued under one auth request must not be redeemable in a different auth request context (state swap / cross-session splicing).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code from victim session was redeemable in attacker session context (state/session splicing) instead of being rejected.
Even though the spliced redemption should fail, the platform still returned a usable identity (flow not atomic / step skipping).

description: Case confusion attack: attempt to collapse two security-distinct principals by varying username case in password grant (e.g., 'Admin' vs 'admin').
invariant_hypothesis: I4: If the upstream principal identifier is case-sensitive, Dex must not normalize case in a way that maps distinct principals to the same downstream subject.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals

oracle_checks.assertion: user_A_entity_id != user_B_entity_id AND user_A_http_status == 200 AND user_B_http_status == 200
oracle_checks.violation_description: Case-variant usernames mapped to the same downstream identity (principal binding collapse)

description: Unicode normalization attack: attempt to collapse two principals using visually identical but byte-distinct usernames (NFC vs NFD), e.g., 'café' vs 'cafe\u0301'.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Dex must not apply Unicode normalization/stringprep that collapses security-distinct upstream principals into the same downstream subject unless explicitly intended by upstream policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals

oracle_checks.assertion: user_B_entity_id != user_C_entity_id AND user_B_http_status == 200 AND user_C_http_status == 200
oracle_checks.violation_description: Unicode NFC/NFD variants mapped to the same downstream identity (normalization-induced principal collision)

description: Token-exchange principal swap: exchange two different upstream subject_tokens via the same OIDC connector and verify Dex does not collapse them into the same downstream identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals (different subject tokens) must map to distinct downstream subjects after RFC8693 token exchange through the OIDC connector.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals

oracle_checks.assertion: user_A_exchanged_entity_id != user_B_exchanged_entity_id AND user_A_exchanged_http_status == 200 AND user_B_exchanged_http_status == 200
oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange collapsed two distinct upstream subject_tokens into the same downstream identity (principal binding failure)

description: Attempt to collapse a normal user and an 'empty/whitespace' principal into the same downstream subject via password grant username edge-cases.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals (normal username vs empty/whitespace username) must not map to the same downstream subject; empty/whitespace must be rejected or mapped distinctly.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals

oracle_checks.assertion: user_attacker_empty_login_status >= 400 OR (user_attacker_empty_entity_id != user_A_entity_id AND user_attacker_empty_entity_id != user_B_entity_id)
oracle_checks.violation_description: Empty-username principal was accepted and collapsed into an existing downstream identity

oracle_checks.assertion: user_attacker_space_login_status >= 400 OR (user_attacker_space_entity_id != user_A_entity_id AND user_attacker_space_entity_id != user_B_entity_id)
oracle_checks.violation_description: Whitespace-username principal was accepted and collapsed into an existing downstream identity

description: Cross-protocol identity merge attempt: password-grant user vs OIDC token-exchange user with potentially overlapping email/name; ensure downstream subjects remain distinct.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: A principal authenticated via password grant must not be merged/collapsed with a different upstream OIDC principal during token exchange solely due to shared attributes (e.g., email/name).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
OIDC token-exchange principal collapsed into the password-grant principal's downstream identity (cross-protocol identity merge)

description: Token exchange scope escalation: start with narrow scope (openid email), then exchange the resulting access token requesting expanded scopes (profile groups federated:id). Expect Dex to reject escalation or at least not return extra claims.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Exchanged token must not grant claims/permissions beyond the upstream authorization intent (original scopes) intersected with broker policy; token exchange must not be a scope escalation primitive.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_scope_escalated_login_status >= 400 OR (user_scope_escalated_name is None AND user_scope_escalated_groups is None AND user_scope_escalated_federated_claims is None)
oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange allowed scope escalation: exchanged token was issued and included claims (profile/groups/federated) not present in the original narrow-scope authorization intent.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_scope_base_http_status == 200 AND user_scope_base_email is not None AND user_scope_base_name is None AND user_scope_base_groups is None AND user_scope_base_federated_claims is None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: base login unexpectedly included extra claims beyond requested scopes, making scope-escalation conclusions unreliable.

description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) attempts to override authorization request parameters (client_id/scope/redirect_uri). Expect Dex to reject or ignore it; acceptance could allow authorization intent manipulation.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Authorization intent must be bound to authenticated request parameters; an unsigned request object must not be accepted to expand scopes or change client/audience semantics.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object, which could allow an attacker to manipulate authorization intent (scope/client/audience) without integrity protection.
Control request to /auth failed unexpectedly; request-object results may be inconclusive due to endpoint/config issues.

description: Token exchange requests narrower scope than original; ensure Dex does not leak claims from the original broader authorization (claim minimization / authorization binding).
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Exchanged tokens must not include claims outside the requested scope for the exchange (and broker policy), even if the original subject_token was minted with broader scopes.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange with scope=openid leaked email claim from broader upstream intent; exchanged token exceeded requested scope.
Token exchange with scope=openid leaked profile/name claim from broader upstream intent; exchanged token exceeded requested scope.
Token exchange with scope=openid leaked groups claim from broader upstream intent; exchanged token exceeded requested scope.
Token exchange with scope=openid leaked federated_claims from broader upstream intent; exchanged token exceeded requested scope.

description: Attempt to mint a refresh-capable token via token exchange by requesting offline_access when the original login did not request it.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not grant offline_access/refresh capability unless it was part of the upstream authorization intent and allowed by broker policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login without offline_access unexpectedly received a refresh_token; upstream intent/broker policy may be over-granting.
Token exchange escalated to offline_access (refresh capability) despite original authorization lacking offline_access.

description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) attempts to override scope to include privileged scopes; ensure Dex rejects or ignores it and does not grant extra claims.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Authorization request parameters (scope/audience) must be bound to authenticated request semantics; an unsigned request object must not expand effective permissions beyond broker policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) was accepted; could allow scope/permission expansion beyond broker policy.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_victim_min_scope_http_status == 200 AND user_victim_min_scope_email is None AND user_victim_min_scope_name is None AND user_victim_min_scope_groups is None AND user_victim_min_scope_federated_claims is None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Minimal-scope login unexpectedly returned extra claims (email/profile/groups/federated_claims), indicating authorization binding failure.

description: Attempt to exchange a victim's subject_token while authenticated as attacker, probing whether token exchange improperly binds effective permissions to the caller rather than the subject_token's upstream intent.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not allow a caller to obtain an exchanged token representing a different upstream principal (victim) or otherwise exceed the upstream intent carried by the submitted subject_token.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange allowed attacker to obtain a token representing the victim (subject_token principal), violating authorization binding to upstream intent.

description: Attempt to use an unsigned request object (alg=none) to override requested scope to include privileged scopes, probing whether Dex incorrectly honors it and grants extra claims/permissions.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Authorization request parameters (scope/audience) must be bound to authenticated upstream intent and broker policy; unsigned request objects must not expand effective permissions.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) was accepted and altered authorization request handling, potentially expanding effective permissions beyond upstream intent.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_reqobj_attack_pwd_groups is None AND user_reqobj_attack_pwd_federated_claims is None AND user_reqobj_attack_pwd_name is None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Privileged claims (groups/profile/federated) appeared without requesting corresponding scopes, indicating authorization binding failure.
